name: Fraxel Repair

lead: Fraxel Repair is the strongest laser in the Fraxel family: a 10,600 nm fractional CO2 laser that removes tiny columns of skin to trigger renewal. It is used for wrinkles around the mouth and eyes, photoaging and scars.
Wikipedia describes it as ablative, in contrast with the non-ablative 1,550 nm Fraxel Restore.

paras: A clinician treats the face in a procedure room; the fractional pattern leaves surrounding skin intact to speed healing. Results build as the skin renews over weeks.
A study of 961 Fraxel treatments reported complications including acne and herpes outbreaks, and anecdotal reports describe scarring and hyperpigmentation.

chain: Fractional CO2 pattern removes microscopic skin columns
angle.text: People use it for noticeable resurfacing of lines and scars. Because it is ablative, it is a heavier procedure than non-ablative lasers.

lead: Fraxel is a line of lasers developed by Reliant Technologies in 2004 from a patent licensed from the Wellman Center for Photomedicine, with R. Rox Anderson named as inventor [1]. They produce fractional photothermolysis for skin resurfacing [1].

Repair is the ablative member of the family, using a 10,600 nm CO2 laser, and is the strongest of the three; it is often used for wrinkles around the mouth or eyes [1]. Restore is a non-ablative 1,550 nm erbium glass laser and Restore Dual adds a 1,927 nm thulium laser [1].
Uses across the line include hyperpigmentation, dark spots, fine lines, wrinkles and acne scarring [1].

paras: Restore (1,550 nm, non-ablative) is the mildest for texture and mild wrinkles; Restore Dual adds a 1,927 nm ablative laser; Repair (10,600 nm CO2) is strongest [1].
A study of 961 treatments reported acne and herpes outbreaks, with anecdotal reports of scarring and hyperpigmentation [1].
No studies found among the cited sources.
